newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INCE SENT OFF BUT INTER STILL GO TOP IN SERIE A.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INCE SENT OFF BUT INTER STILL GO TOP IN SERIE A.

text.p: Internazionale, down to 10 men after England midfielder Paul Ince was sent off in the first half, beat Piacenza 2-0 on Saturday to go top in Italy's serie A while champions Milan slumped to a rare 3-0 defeat at Roma.
Inter now have 11 points from five matches. European Cup holders Juventus, who have 10 points, will regain the lead on Sunday if they win at Vicenza.

Ince was sent off in the 37th minute, just after Inter's French striker Youri Djourkaeff missed a controversial penalty and Piacenza goalkeeper Massimo Taibi, who committed the original penalty foul, saved Ince's rebound shot.
The Englishman was ruled to have felled Piacenza's Gianpietro Piovani with a blow as players waited for a corner.
Piovani was himself sent off in the dying seconds for elbowing an opponent.
Inter went ahead eight minutes later when Marco Branca headed in off a corner and consolidated their lead in the 47th when Djorkaeff made amends for the missed penalty with an excellent solo goal.
Roma, who had not beaten ancient foes Milan in a league match at the Olympic Stadium for more than 10 years, stunned the visitors with two early goals in the space of six minutes.
Striker Francesco Totti beat Sebastiano Rossi to a high ball on the right of the area in the 13th minute and sent a looping shot across the goalmouth and into the net.
Massimiliano Cappioli made it 2-0 in the 19th minute, tapping in a beautifully timed cross from Argentine striker Abelo Balbo that left Rossi wrong-footed.
Balbo made it 3-0 in the 89th minute as the capacity crowd hailed their heroes with chants of "Ole, Ole".
Milan looked wobbly in defence, despite the return of veteran defender Franco Baresi, while attackers Roberto Baggio and George Weah had a frustrating night.

The match was also billed as a clash between Latin American coaches with Roma's Argentine Carlos Bianchi, who also beat Milan with Velez Sarsfeld in the 1994 Intercontinental Cup, winning out over Milan's Uruguayan Oscar Tabarez.
In the day's third match, Fiorentina and Lazio drew 0-0 with Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta missing a penalty for Fiorentina while Lazio goalkeeper Luca Marchegiani made several dramatic saves.
The topsy-turvy match saw rapid counter-attacks for much of the first half but none of the handful of top international strikers on the pitch could put the ball in the net.

Brazilian-born Luis Oliveira, who plays for Belgium, proved fresher than tired team mate Batistuta, still recovering from Argentina's World Cup victory over Venezuela this week, but wasted several chances in front of Marchigiani.

But Lazio's Giuseppe Signori and Pierluigi Casiraghi, who was repeatedly wide of the mark for Italy against Georgia in midweek, blew just as many opportunities in front of fellow international goalkeeper Francesco Toldo.
Batistuta, whose form has been surprisingly lacklustre this season, lofted a 34th minute penalty over the bar after his cross was handled by defender Giuseppe Favalli.
